# synesis-help

## Description

Role in the ecosystem: **reference guide (people and agents)**

Run without arguments for the keyboard-driven guide. Agents and scripts use the JSON contract:

- `synesis-help search <words> --format=json` finds entries by text;
- `synesis-help lookup <ID or term> --format=json` returns one entry (with suggestions when nothing matches exactly);
- `synesis-help list [--category <name>] --format=json` shows what exists.

Exit codes: 0 found, 1 not found, 2 usage error. Every JSON answer carries `help_version` and `synesis_version` (the compiler the generated entries were derived from), so an agent can tell whether the guide matches the installed compiler.

## Usage

```text
usage: synesis-help [-h] [--version]
                    {build,lookup,search,list,docs,credits} ...

Quick reference guide to the Synesis language, for people and agents.

positional arguments:
  {build,lookup,search,list,docs,credits}
    build               compile the entries into the SQLite index
    lookup              show one entry (ID, title or term)
    search              full-text search over all entries
    list                list the entries, optionally of one category
    docs                how to write and fix entries
    credits             authorship, license and how to cite

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --version             show program's version number and exit

examples:
  synesis-help                              open the guide (TUI)
  synesis-help lookup CHAIN                 one entry in the terminal
  synesis-help lookup E047 --format=json    one entry, JSON contract
  synesis-help search bundle status         full-text search
  synesis-help list --category case_study   what exists in a category
  synesis-help docs                         how to write and fix entries
  synesis-help credits                      authorship, license and how to cite

for agents:
  use --format=json; exit codes are 0 found, 1 not found, 2 usage error;
  every answer carries help_version and synesis_version.

in the guide:
  arrows  move / scroll            F2   cross-references
  Enter   go forward               F3   incremental search
  Tab     switch panel             Esc  quit
```

For the options of a subcommand: `synesis-help <command> --help`.
